newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES CLOSE WEEK STABLE.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES CLOSE WEEK STABLE.

text.p: Zimbabwe's short-term trading rates were quoted steady at their previous levels in quiet Friday trade, dealers said.
The market opened Z$226.5 million short but was forecast to close with a Z$107 million surplus on the back of maturities.
But the central Reserve Bank did not come into the market on Friday with an auction for treasury bills to mop up the excess liquidity as is the norm.
However the central bank bills were being traded on the secondary market at 24.80 percent, unchanged from Thursday, while call money ranged between 24 and 26 percent.

NCDs maturing after 30, 60 and 90 days were being bought at 26.75 percent and sold at 26 percent while bankers acceptance bills were stable at 25.5 percent (buying) and at 25 percent on the selling side.
